manifest.title: (μ,ε)-Robustness: Characterization, Existence, and Precision-Dependent Bounds

inputs.abstract:
Covering criteria characterize relaxed robustness on semimetric spaces. For
finite totally ordered spaces, boundary criteria characterize triviality, and
every $(\mu,\varepsilon)$-robust partition is trivial when
$\varepsilon\ge\Delta\delta\mu+\Delta$. Triviality transfers through finite
$\mu$-closed overlapping decompositions. Restriction and union admit
counterexamples. Canonical binary floats,
sum products, synchronized maximum products, and padded lists provide ordered
semimetric constructions.

concepts.title: ε-Ball
concepts.description:
A closed ball consists of all inputs within a chosen distance of its center, including inputs exactly at that distance.

**Definition from the paper.**

Let $(S,d)$ be a semimetric space. Then

$$B(x^*,\epsilon):=\{x\in S\mid d(x,x^*)\leq\epsilon\}$$

is an **$\epsilon$-ball** around $x^*$.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
Closed inequalities are essential: an input at distance exactly ε must have the same label. Ball membership uses d(x,x*), matching the paper; Lean spells the center `x_star`.

The auxiliary neighborhood of a set $A$ is $\bigcup_{x\in A}B(x,r)$.

import Lax544225.SemimetricSpace
import Mathlib.Data.Set.Lattice

/-!
---
title: ε-Ball
type: definition
---
A closed ball consists of all inputs within a chosen distance of its center, including inputs exactly at that distance.

**Definition from the paper.**

Let $(S,d)$ be a semimetric space. Then

$$B(x^*,\epsilon):=\{x\in S\mid d(x,x^*)\leq\epsilon\}$$

is an **$\epsilon$-ball** around $x^*$.

# Formalization notes

Closed inequalities are essential: an input at distance exactly ε must have the same label. Ball membership uses d(x,x*), matching the paper; Lean spells the center `x_star`.

The auxiliary neighborhood of a set $A$ is $\bigcup_{x\in A}B(x,r)$.
-/

universe u

namespace Lax544225.Balls

open scoped NNReal

open SemimetricSpace
/-- The closed ε-ball centered at the paper’s point x*. -/
def ball {S : Type u} (d : Distance S) (_hd : IsSemimetricSpace d)
    (x_star : S) (ε : ℝ≥0) : Set S :=
  {x | d x x_star ≤ ε}

/-- The union of closed r-balls with centers in A. -/
def neighborhood {S : Type u} (d : Distance S) (hd : IsSemimetricSpace d)
    (A : Set S) (r : ℝ≥0) : Set S :=
  {y | ∃ x ∈ A, y ∈ ball d hd x r}

end Lax544225.Balls

concepts.title: Binary Floating Point Format
concepts.description:
A binary floating-point format specifies a precision and a range of exponents. Its finite values are supplemented by signed zeros, signed infinities, and one NaN. A real-valued embedding assigns distinct positions to these special values.

**Definition from the paper.**

Let $\mathcal F$ be a binary floating point format with $p\in\mathbb N$
mantissa bits. Its finite nonzero values are triples $(s,c,m)$ representing
$(-1)^s2^cm$, where $s\in\{0,1\}$,
$c\in\{c_{\min},\dots,c_{\max}\}\subset\mathbb Z$, and

$$m\in\{k2^{-p}\mid k\in\{1,\dots,2^{p+1}-1\}\}.$$

Each triple satisfies either $m\geq1$ (normal) or $c=c_{\min}$ (subnormal).
The format also contains $\pm0$, $\mathrm{NaN}$ and $\pm\mathrm{Inf}$.
Define $\phi:\mathcal F\rightarrow\mathbb R$ by

- $\phi((s,c,m))=(-1)^s2^cm$;
- $\phi(+0)=0$ and $\phi(-0)=-2^{c_{\min}-p-1}$;
- $\phi(\mathrm{NaN})=2^{c_{\max}+1}+1$;
- $\phi(\pm\mathrm{Inf})=\pm2^{c_{\max}+1}$.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown: This is the paper’s single-NaN abstraction, matching the supplied Flocq BinarySingleNaN examples, not the full set of IEEE NaN payloads. A finite mantissa is stored as the integer k with m=k·2^(−p); normality means k≥2^p. The independent order puts −∞ first, then negative finite values, −0, +0, positive finite values, +∞, and NaN. It is not defined by φ.

import Lax544225.OrderedSemimetric
import Mathlib.Data.Real.Basic
import Mathlib.Data.Int.Cast.Lemmas

/-!
---
title: Binary Floating Point Format
type: definition
---
A binary floating-point format specifies a precision and a range of exponents. Its finite values are supplemented by signed zeros, signed infinities, and one NaN. A real-valued embedding assigns distinct positions to these special values.

**Definition from the paper.**

Let $\mathcal F$ be a binary floating point format with $p\in\mathbb N$
mantissa bits. Its finite nonzero values are triples $(s,c,m)$ representing
$(-1)^s2^cm$, where $s\in\{0,1\}$,
$c\in\{c_{\min},\dots,c_{\max}\}\subset\mathbb Z$, and

$$m\in\{k2^{-p}\mid k\in\{1,\dots,2^{p+1}-1\}\}.$$

Each triple satisfies either $m\geq1$ (normal) or $c=c_{\min}$ (subnormal).
The format also contains $\pm0$, $\mathrm{NaN}$ and $\pm\mathrm{Inf}$.
Define $\phi:\mathcal F\rightarrow\mathbb R$ by

- $\phi((s,c,m))=(-1)^s2^cm$;
- $\phi(+0)=0$ and $\phi(-0)=-2^{c_{\min}-p-1}$;
- $\phi(\mathrm{NaN})=2^{c_{\max}+1}+1$;
- $\phi(\pm\mathrm{Inf})=\pm2^{c_{\max}+1}$.

# Formalization notes

This is the paper’s single-NaN abstraction, matching the supplied Flocq BinarySingleNaN examples, not the full set of IEEE NaN payloads. A finite mantissa is stored as the integer k with m=k·2^(−p); normality means k≥2^p. The independent order puts −∞ first, then negative finite values, −0, +0, positive finite values, +∞, and NaN. It is not defined by φ.
-/

universe u

namespace Lax544225.BinaryFloats

open scoped NNReal

/-- The precision and nonempty exponent interval of a binary format. -/
structure Format where
  /-- Number of fractional bits in the significand. -/
  precision : ℕ
  /-- Least allowed exponent. -/
  minExponent : ℤ
  /-- Greatest allowed exponent. -/
  maxExponent : ℤ
  /-- The exponent interval is nonempty. -/
  exponent_le : minExponent ≤ maxExponent

/-- Canonical data for a nonzero finite number in a format. -/
structure FiniteValue (F : Format) where
  /-- Sign bit: 0 is positive and 1 is negative. -/
  sign : Fin 2
  /-- The exponent of the value. -/
  exponent : ℤ
  /-- The integer significand before scaling by 2^(−p). -/
  mantissa : ℕ
  /-- The exponent is allowed by the format. -/
  exponent_mem : F.minExponent ≤ exponent ∧ exponent ≤ F.maxExponent
  /-- The significand is nonzero and less than 2^(p+1). -/
  mantissa_mem : 0 < mantissa ∧ mantissa < 2 ^ (F.precision + 1)
  /-- A significand below the normal range occurs only at the minimum exponent. -/
  canonical : 2 ^ F.precision ≤ mantissa ∨ exponent = F.minExponent

/-- Canonical finite data and the four signed special values together with one NaN. -/
inductive Value (F : Format)
  /-- A nonzero finite floating-point value. -/
  | finite : FiniteValue F → Value F
  /-- A signed zero. -/
  | zero : Fin 2 → Value F
  /-- A signed infinity. -/
  | infinity : Fin 2 → Value F
  /-- The single, greatest NaN value. -/
  | nan : Value F

/-- The exact ordinary real value of canonical finite data. -/
noncomputable def finiteReal {F : Format} (f : FiniteValue F) : ℝ :=
  (-1 : ℝ) ^ f.sign.val * (2 : ℝ) ^ f.exponent *
    ((f.mantissa : ℝ) * (2 : ℝ) ^ (-(F.precision : ℤ)))

/-- The real embedding including separated signed zeros and bounded special values. -/
noncomputable def phi (F : Format) : Value F → ℝ
  | .finite f => finiteReal f
  | .zero s => if s.val = 0 then 0 else -(2 : ℝ) ^ (F.minExponent - (F.precision : ℤ) - 1)
  | .infinity s => if s.val = 0 then (2 : ℝ) ^ (F.maxExponent + 1)
    else -(2 : ℝ) ^ (F.maxExponent + 1)
  | .nan => (2 : ℝ) ^ (F.maxExponent + 1) + 1

/-- The position of each sign and special-value category in the total order. -/
def category {F : Format} : Value F → ℕ
  | .finite f => if f.sign.val = 0 then 4 else 1
  | .zero s => if s.val = 0 then 3 else 2
  | .infinity s => if s.val = 0 then 5 else 0
  | .nan => 6

/-- The ordinary finite value used to order members within a finite category. -/
noncomputable def withinCategory {F : Format} : Value F → ℝ
  | .finite f => finiteReal f
  | _ => 0

/-- IEEE category order with one positive NaN and exact comparison of finite values. -/
def ieeeLe (F : Format) (x y : Value F) : Prop :=
  category x < category y ∨
    (category x = category y ∧ withinCategory x ≤ withinCategory y)

end Lax544225.BinaryFloats

concepts.title: Successor and Boundary
concepts.description:
An immediate successor is the next point in the order, with no point in between. The boundary of a subset consists of its points adjacent to points outside it; the complement has its own boundary.

**Definition from the paper.**

In a totally ordered semimetric space $(S,<,d)$, $Succ(x,y)$ holds if
$x<y$ and there is no $z$ with $x<z<y$.
For each subset $S'\subseteq S$, its **boundary** is

$$\partial S':=\{x\in S'\mid\exists y\notin S',\ Succ(x,y)\lor Succ(y,x)\},$$

and its **complement boundary** is

$$\overline{\partial}S':=\{x\notin S'\mid\exists y\in S',\ Succ(x,y)\lor Succ(y,x)\}.$$

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown: Successor is the standard mathlib cover relation `CovBy`, with the paper's name retained as an alias.

import Lax544225.Balls
import Mathlib.Order.Cover

/-!
---
title: Successor and Boundary
type: definition
---
An immediate successor is the next point in the order, with no point in between. The boundary of a subset consists of its points adjacent to points outside it; the complement has its own boundary.

**Definition from the paper.**

In a totally ordered semimetric space $(S,<,d)$, $Succ(x,y)$ holds if
$x<y$ and there is no $z$ with $x<z<y$.
For each subset $S'\subseteq S$, its **boundary** is

$$\partial S':=\{x\in S'\mid\exists y\notin S',\ Succ(x,y)\lor Succ(y,x)\},$$

and its **complement boundary** is

$$\overline{\partial}S':=\{x\notin S'\mid\exists y\in S',\ Succ(x,y)\lor Succ(y,x)\}.$$

# Formalization notes

Successor is the standard mathlib cover relation `CovBy`, with the paper's name retained as an alias.

-/

universe u

namespace Lax544225.Boundary

open scoped NNReal

open SemimetricSpace Balls
/-- Consecutive points in a linear order. -/
abbrev Successor {S : Type u} [LinearOrder S] (x y : S) : Prop :=
  CovBy x y

/-- Points of S' adjacent to its complement in the ambient order. -/
def boundary {S : Type u} [LinearOrder S] (S' : Set S) : Set S :=
  {x | x ∈ S' ∧ ∃ y ∈ S'ᶜ, Successor x y ∨ Successor y x}

/-- Points outside S' adjacent to S' in the ambient order. -/
def complementBoundary {S : Type u} [LinearOrder S] (S' : Set S) : Set S :=
  boundary S'ᶜ

end Lax544225.Boundary

concepts.title: Theorem 3 — Boundary covering characterization
concepts.description:
In a finite ordered space, the covering criterion can be expressed using the boundaries of the two sides of each cut.

**Statement from the paper.**

Let $(S,<,d)$ be a finite totally ordered semimetric space and
$\mu\geq0$, $\epsilon>0$. The following statements are equivalent:

1. For every nonempty proper subset $S'\subset S$, there exists $x\in S$
   such that either

   $$x\in S'\quad\text{and}\quad B(x,\mu)\subseteq\bigcup_{x'\in S\setminus S'}B(x',\epsilon),$$

   or

   $$x\in S\setminus S'\quad\text{and}\quad B(x,\mu)\subseteq\bigcup_{x'\in S'}B(x',\epsilon).$$

2. For every nonempty proper subset $S'\subset S$, there exists $x\in S$
   such that either

   $$x\in S'\quad\text{and}\quad B(x,\mu)\cap S'\subseteq\bigcup_{x'\in\overline{\partial}S'}B(x',\epsilon),$$

   or

   $$x\in S\setminus S'\quad\text{and}\quad B(x,\mu)\cap(S\setminus S')\subseteq\bigcup_{x'\in\partial S'}B(x',\epsilon).$$

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
Both directions are stated together as in the paper. Their separate arguments
remain supporting lemmas in the proof package.

title: Theorem 3 — Boundary covering characterization
type: theorem
---
In a finite ordered space, the covering criterion can be expressed using the boundaries of the two sides of each cut.

**Statement from the paper.**

Let $(S,<,d)$ be a finite totally ordered semimetric space and
$\mu\geq0$, $\epsilon>0$. The following statements are equivalent:

1. For every nonempty proper subset $S'\subset S$, there exists $x\in S$
   such that either

   $$x\in S'\quad\text{and}\quad B(x,\mu)\subseteq\bigcup_{x'\in S\setminus S'}B(x',\epsilon),$$

   or

   $$x\in S\setminus S'\quad\text{and}\quad B(x,\mu)\subseteq\bigcup_{x'\in S'}B(x',\epsilon).$$

2. For every nonempty proper subset $S'\subset S$, there exists $x\in S$
   such that either

   $$x\in S'\quad\text{and}\quad B(x,\mu)\cap S'\subseteq\bigcup_{x'\in\overline{\partial}S'}B(x',\epsilon),$$

   or

   $$x\in S\setminus S'\quad\text{and}\quad B(x,\mu)\cap(S\setminus S')\subseteq\bigcup_{x'\in\partial S'}B(x',\epsilon).$$

# Formalization notes

Both directions are stated together as in the paper. Their separate arguments
remain supporting lemmas in the proof package.
-/

universe u

namespace Lax544225.BoundaryCoveringCharacterization

open scoped NNReal
open SemimetricSpace OrderedSemimetric Balls Boundary

/-- In a finite totally ordered semimetric space, covering every proper cut is equivalent to covering its within-side μ-ball from the opposite boundary. -/
axiom statement {S : Type u} [Finite S] [LinearOrder S] (d : Distance S)
    (hd : IsOrderedSemimetricSpace d (· ≤ ·)) (μ : ℝ≥0) (ε : ℝ>0) :
    (∀ S' : Set S, S'.Nonempty → S'ᶜ.Nonempty →
      ∃ x, (x ∈ S' ∧ ball d hd.1 x μ ⊆ neighborhood d hd.1 S'ᶜ ε) ∨
        (x ∈ S'ᶜ ∧ ball d hd.1 x μ ⊆ neighborhood d hd.1 S' ε)) ↔ (∀ S' : Set S, S'.Nonempty → S'ᶜ.Nonempty →
      ∃ x, (x ∈ S' ∧ ball d hd.1 x μ ∩ S' ⊆ neighborhood d hd.1 (complementBoundary S') ε) ∨
        (x ∈ S'ᶜ ∧ ball d hd.1 x μ ∩ S'ᶜ ⊆ neighborhood d hd.1 (boundary S') ε))

end Lax544225.BoundaryCoveringCharacterization

concepts.title: Classifier
concepts.description:
A classifier assigns a class to every input, and every class occurs for at least one input.

**Definition from the paper.**

Let $S$ be a set of inputs and $[n]$ a set of classes. A **classifier** is a
total, surjective function $c:S\rightarrow[n]$.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown: Fin n labels the classes from 0 to n−1; adding 1 recovers the paper’s labels 1 to n. Surjectivity is retained. Existence of a classifier on a nonempty carrier implies n > 0.

concepts.title: Theorem 1 — Covering characterization of robustness
concepts.description:
A partition is robust exactly when every input has a nearby point that stays beyond the robustness radius of all points outside its part.

**Statement from the paper.**

Let $(S,d)$ be a semimetric space, $P:=\{S_1,\dots,S_n\}$ a partition of $S$,
and $\mu\geq0$, $\epsilon>0$. The following are equivalent:

1. $P$ is $(\mu,\epsilon)$-robust.
2. For all $S_i\in P$ and all $x\in S_i$,

   $$B(x,\mu)\not\subseteq\bigcup_{x^*\in S\setminus S_i}B(x^*,\epsilon).$$

concepts.title: (μ,ε)-Decomposition
concepts.description:
A decomposition covers the space by pieces that contain every sufficiently nearby point of each of their members. Overlapping pieces form chains connecting any two inputs.

**Definition from the paper.**

A collection of nonempty sets $D:=\{D_1,\dots,D_p\}$ is a
**$(\mu,\epsilon)$-decomposition** of a semimetric space $(S,d)$ if and only if

1. For each $x\in D_i$, $B(x,\mu)\subseteq D_i$.
2. For each $x_1,x_2\in S$, there is a sequence of sets
   $D_{i_1},\dots,D_{i_n}\in D$ such that
   $D_{i_j}\cap D_{i_{j+1}}\neq\emptyset$ for consecutive members,
   $x_1\in D_{i_1}$, and $x_2\in D_{i_n}$.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown: The definition depends only on μ; ε appears in the applications. ReflTransGen encodes a finite chain, including a chain consisting of a single member. Membership of each endpoint member and each link is explicit. Finiteness concerns the family, not the sizes of its members.

import Lax544225.Balls

import Mathlib.Data.Set.Finite.Basic

/-!
---
title: (μ,ε)-Decomposition
type: definition
---
A decomposition covers the space by pieces that contain every sufficiently nearby point of each of their members. Overlapping pieces form chains connecting any two inputs.

**Definition from the paper.**

A collection of nonempty sets $D:=\{D_1,\dots,D_p\}$ is a
**$(\mu,\epsilon)$-decomposition** of a semimetric space $(S,d)$ if and only if

1. For each $x\in D_i$, $B(x,\mu)\subseteq D_i$.
2. For each $x_1,x_2\in S$, there is a sequence of sets
   $D_{i_1},\dots,D_{i_n}\in D$ such that
   $D_{i_j}\cap D_{i_{j+1}}\neq\emptyset$ for consecutive members,
   $x_1\in D_{i_1}$, and $x_2\in D_{i_n}$.

# Formalization notes

The definition depends only on μ; ε appears in the applications. ReflTransGen encodes a finite chain, including a chain consisting of a single member. Membership of each endpoint member and each link is explicit. Finiteness concerns the family, not the sizes of its members.
-/

namespace Lax544225.Decomposition

open scoped NNReal

open SemimetricSpace Balls
/-- A finite family of nonempty μ-closed pieces connected by overlaps. -/
def IsDecomposition {S : Type u} (d : Distance S) (hd : IsSemimetricSpace d)
    (D : Set (Set S)) (μ : ℝ≥0) : Prop :=
  D.Finite ∧ (∀ A ∈ D, A.Nonempty) ∧
    (∀ A ∈ D, ∀ x ∈ A, ball d hd x μ ⊆ A) ∧
    (∀ x y, ∃ A ∈ D, ∃ B ∈ D, x ∈ A ∧ y ∈ B ∧
      Relation.ReflTransGen (fun C E => C ∈ D ∧ E ∈ D ∧ (C ∩ E).Nonempty) A B)

end Lax544225.Decomposition

concepts.title: ε-Robustness
concepts.description:
Local robustness means that all inputs sufficiently close to a given input have the same label. Global robustness requires this at every input. Relaxed robustness allows each input to move a short distance to a locally robust input with the same label.

**Definition from the paper.**

Let $(S,d)$ be a semimetric space. A classifier $c:S\rightarrow[n]$ is
**locally robust** at a point $x^*\in S$ for $\epsilon>0$ if

$$\forall x\in S\;[d(x,x^*)\leq\epsilon\rightarrow c(x)=c(x^*)].$$

The classifier is **globally $\epsilon$-robust** if it is locally
$\epsilon$-robust at every point.

The classifier is **$(\mu,\epsilon)$-robust**, for
$\mu\in\mathbb{R}_{\geq0}$ and $\epsilon\in\mathbb{R}_{>0}$, if for every
$x\in S$ there exists $x'\in S$ with $d(x,x')\leq\mu$ such that
$c(x)=c(x')$ and $c$ is locally $\epsilon$-robust at $x'$.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown: Each predicate requires evidence that the distance defines a semimetric space. The parameter types encode μ ≥ 0 and ε > 0 directly: `μ : ℝ≥0` and `ε : ℝ>0`. The latter is the subtype of strictly positive real numbers; no separate positivity hypothesis is needed. No robustness predicate can be applied at ε=0. The same-label requirement is present even when μ>ε. In Lean, `x_star` denotes the paper’s reference point $x^*$ and `x` the quantified input. Both robustness definitions use the paper’s distance inequalities directly; their ball characterizations are proved in the proof package.

namespace Lax544225.EpsilonRobustness

open scoped NNReal

open Classifier SemimetricSpace
/-- Local robustness at the paper’s reference point x*. -/
def LocallyEpsilonRobust {S : Type u} {n : ℕ} (d : Distance S) (_hd : IsSemimetricSpace d)
    (c : Classifier S n) (ε : ℝ>0) (x_star : S) : Prop :=
  ∀ x, d x x_star ≤ ε → c.label x = c.label x_star

/-- Local robustness at every input. -/
def GloballyEpsilonRobust {S : Type u} {n : ℕ} (d : Distance S) (hd : IsSemimetricSpace d)
    (c : Classifier S n) (ε : ℝ>0) : Prop :=
  ∀ x, LocallyEpsilonRobust d hd c ε x

/-- (μ,ε)-robustness: each input is μ-close to a same-label locally ε-robust input. -/
def MuEpsilonRobust {S : Type u} {n : ℕ} (d : Distance S) (hd : IsSemimetricSpace d)
    (c : Classifier S n) (μ : ℝ≥0) (ε : ℝ>0) : Prop :=
  ∀ x, ∃ x', d x x' ≤ μ ∧ c.label x = c.label x' ∧ LocallyEpsilonRobust d hd c ε x'

end Lax544225.EpsilonRobustness

concepts.description:
The distance between two floating-point values is the absolute difference of their real embeddings. Together with the IEEE total order, it forms an ordered semimetric space.

Let $\mathcal F$ and $\phi$ be the binary floating-point format and embedding defined above. Set

$$d_1(f_1,f_2):=|\phi(f_1)-\phi(f_2)|.$$

Then $(\mathcal F,<_{IEEE},d_1)$ is an ordered semimetric space, where $<_{IEEE}$ is the IEEE total order.

concepts.title: Theorem 2 — General existence criterion
concepts.description:
The possibility of a nontrivial robust partition is determined by how balls on opposite sides of a cut cover one another.

**Statement from the paper.**

Let $(S,d)$ be a semimetric space and $\mu\geq0$, $\epsilon>0$.
The following statements are equivalent:

1. The only $(\mu,\epsilon)$-robust partition on $S$ is trivial.
2. For every nonempty proper subset $S'\subset S$, there exists $x\in S$
   such that either

   $$x\in S'\quad\text{and}\quad B(x,\mu)\subseteq\bigcup_{x'\in S\setminus S'}B(x',\epsilon),$$

   or

   $$x\in S\setminus S'\quad\text{and}\quad B(x,\mu)\subseteq\bigcup_{x'\in S'}B(x',\epsilon).$$

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
Both directions are stated together as in the paper. Their separate arguments
remain supporting lemmas in the proof package.

concepts.title: Finite List Distances and Orders
concepts.description:
For lists of different lengths, missing entries are filled with a padding value before comparing coordinates, and a unit penalty distinguishes different lengths. The orders compare only lists of equal length.

**Definition from the paper.**

The sum and maximum product distances extend to arbitrary finite lists of
floating-point numbers. For distance computation, the shorter list is padded
with $\mathrm{NaN}$, and a penalty equal to $1$ is added whenever the list
lengths differ. The partial orders compare only lists of the same length;
lists of different lengths are incomparable.
Both extensions are ordered semimetric spaces: the sum extension assumes an
ordered semimetric base, and the maximum extension additionally assumes
additivity along ordered chains.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
The floating-point instance chooses NaN as padding. Without the length penalty, appending NaN would give distance zero between different lists. The list maximum construction uses an additive base distance just as the fixed-length construction does.

The definitions allow an arbitrary base space and padding point, specializing to the paper by choosing floating-point values and NaN.

/-!
---
title: Finite List Distances and Orders
type: definition
---
For lists of different lengths, missing entries are filled with a padding value before comparing coordinates, and a unit penalty distinguishes different lengths. The orders compare only lists of equal length.

**Definition from the paper.**

The sum and maximum product distances extend to arbitrary finite lists of
floating-point numbers. For distance computation, the shorter list is padded
with $\mathrm{NaN}$, and a penalty equal to $1$ is added whenever the list
lengths differ. The partial orders compare only lists of the same length;
lists of different lengths are incomparable.
Both extensions are ordered semimetric spaces: the sum extension assumes an
ordered semimetric base, and the maximum extension additionally assumes
additivity along ordered chains.

# Formalization notes

The floating-point instance chooses NaN as padding. Without the length penalty, appending NaN would give distance zero between different lists. The list maximum construction uses an additive base distance just as the fixed-length construction does.

The definitions allow an arbitrary base space and padding point, specializing to the paper by choosing floating-point values and NaN.
-/

universe u

namespace Lax544225.ListSpaces

open scoped NNReal

open SemimetricSpace OrderedSemimetric
open scoped BigOperators
/-- Equal-length lists ordered coordinatewise; other lengths are incomparable. -/
def listLe {S : Type u} (le : S → S → Prop) (pad : S) (f g : List S) : Prop :=
  f.length = g.length ∧ ∀ i < f.length, le (f.getD i pad) (g.getD i pad)

/-- Equal-length coordinatewise order with equal base distances across coordinates. -/
def synchronizedListLe {S : Type u} (d : Distance S) (le : S → S → Prop)
    (pad : S) (f g : List S) : Prop :=
  listLe le pad f g ∧ ∀ i < f.length, ∀ j < f.length,
    d (f.getD i pad) (g.getD i pad) = d (f.getD j pad) (g.getD j pad)

/-- A positive penalty that distinguishes different list lengths. -/
def lengthPenalty {S : Type u} (f g : List S) : ℝ≥0 :=
  if f.length = g.length then 0 else 1

/-- Sum of padded coordinate distances, plus the length penalty. -/
noncomputable def sumDistance {S : Type u} (d : Distance S) (pad : S) : Distance (List S) :=
  fun f g => lengthPenalty f g +
    ∑ i ∈ Finset.range (max f.length g.length), d (f.getD i pad) (g.getD i pad)

/-- Maximum padded coordinate distance, plus the length penalty. -/
noncomputable def maxDistance {S : Type u} (d : Distance S) (pad : S) : Distance (List S) :=
  fun f g => lengthPenalty f g +
    (Finset.range (max f.length g.length)).sup (fun i => d (f.getD i pad) (g.getD i pad))

/-- Both padded-list constructions are ordered semimetric spaces. -/
axiom statement :
    (∀ {S : Type u} (d : Distance S) (le : S → S → Prop),
      IsOrderedSemimetricSpace d le → ∀ pad : S,
        IsOrderedSemimetricSpace (Lax544225.ListSpaces.sumDistance d pad) (Lax544225.ListSpaces.listLe le pad)) ∧
    (∀ {S : Type u} (d : Distance S) (le : S → S → Prop),
      IsOrderedSemimetricSpace d le → Additive d le → ∀ pad : S,
        IsOrderedSemimetricSpace (Lax544225.ListSpaces.maxDistance d pad)
          (Lax544225.ListSpaces.synchronizedListLe d le pad))

end Lax544225.ListSpaces

concepts.title: Synchronized Maximum Product Distance
concepts.description:
For tuples, take the greatest coordinate distance. Compare tuples only when each coordinate moves in order by the same distance. The base distance must be additive along ordered chains.

**Definition from the paper.**

Suppose $(\mathcal F,<,d)$ is an ordered semimetric space and
$d(a,c)=d(a,b)+d(b,c)$ whenever $a\leq b\leq c$. Define

$$d_4(f,g):=\max_{i\in[n]}d(f_i,g_i),$$

$$<^n_*:=\{(f,g)\in\mathcal F^n\times\mathcal F^n\mid f<^n g\ \land
\forall i,j\in[n],\ d(f_i,g_i)=d(f_j,g_j)\}.$$

Then $(\mathcal F^n,<^n_*,d_4)$ is an ordered semimetric space.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown: The construction is proved for any base carrier. Coordinates are Fin n; the maximum over no coordinates is zero. The formal relation includes equality, with the paper’s strict notation denoting its strict part.

/-!

title: Synchronized Maximum Product Distance
type: definition
---
For tuples, take the greatest coordinate distance. Compare tuples only when each coordinate moves in order by the same distance. The base distance must be additive along ordered chains.

**Definition from the paper.**

Suppose $(\mathcal F,<,d)$ is an ordered semimetric space and
$d(a,c)=d(a,b)+d(b,c)$ whenever $a\leq b\leq c$. Define

$$d_4(f,g):=\max_{i\in[n]}d(f_i,g_i),$$

$$<^n_*:=\{(f,g)\in\mathcal F^n\times\mathcal F^n\mid f<^n g\ \land
\forall i,j\in[n],\ d(f_i,g_i)=d(f_j,g_j)\}.$$

Then $(\mathcal F^n,<^n_*,d_4)$ is an ordered semimetric space.

# Formalization notes

The construction is proved for any base carrier. Coordinates are Fin n; the maximum over no coordinates is zero. The formal relation includes equality, with the paper’s strict notation denoting its strict part.
-/

namespace Lax544225.MaximumProductSpace

open SemimetricSpace OrderedSemimetric SumProductSpace

/-- Coordinatewise order restricted to equal distances in every coordinate. -/
def synchronizedLe {S : Type u} (d : Distance S) (le : S → S → Prop) (n : ℕ)
    (f g : Fin n → S) : Prop :=
  productLe le n f g ∧ ∀ i j, d (f i) (g i) = d (f j) (g j)

/-- Maximum of the base distances between corresponding coordinates. -/
noncomputable def maxDistance {S : Type u} (d : Distance S) (n : ℕ) : Distance (Fin n → S) :=
  fun f g => Finset.univ.sup (fun i => d (f i) (g i))

/-- Synchronized maximum products preserve ordered semimetric spaces. -/
axiom statement {S : Type u} (d : Distance S) (le : S → S → Prop)
    (hd : IsOrderedSemimetricSpace d le) (hadd : Additive d le) (n : ℕ) :
    IsOrderedSemimetricSpace (maxDistance d n) (synchronizedLe d le n)

end Lax544225.MaximumProductSpace

concepts.title: Lemma 1 — Noncompositionality of robustness
concepts.description:
For a semimetric space $(S,d)$, overlapping proper subsets $S_1,S_2$, and
$\mu\geq 0$, $\epsilon>0$, the following implications are false in general:

1. If only the trivial partition on $S_1$ is $(\mu,\epsilon)$-robust, then every
   $(\mu,\epsilon)$-robust partition of $S$ contains a part including $S_1$.
2. If only the trivial partitions on $S_1$ and $S_2$ are $(\mu,\epsilon)$-robust,
   then only the trivial partition on $S_1\cup S_2$ is $(\mu,\epsilon)$-robust.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
Both implications are refuted by explicit counterexamples on the four-point
line $\{0,1,2,3\}$ with $\mu=\epsilon=1$ and partition
$\{\{0,1\},\{2,3\}\}$. The first uses $S_1=\{1,2\}$; the unused second
subset can be chosen equal to $S_1$. The second uses $S_1=\{0,1,2\}$ and
$S_2=\{1,2,3\}$. The two existential clauses record these counterexamples.

concepts.title: Ordered Semimetric Space
concepts.description:
An ordered semimetric space relates its order to its distance: moving through an intermediate point in the order cannot cost more than the direct distance between the endpoints.

**Definition from the paper.**

A tuple $(S,<,d)$ with a set $S$, a partial order $<$ on $S$, and
$d:S\times S\rightarrow\mathbb{R}_{\geq0}$ is an **ordered semimetric space**
if $(S,d)$ is a semimetric space and, for all $a,b,c\in S$,

$$a\leq b\leq c\quad\Longrightarrow\quad d(a,c)\geq d(a,b)+d(b,c).$$

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
The order is an explicit non-strict relation. Mathlib’s `IsPartialOrder` provides reflexivity, transitivity, and antisymmetry. The reverse triangle inequality is imposed only on ordered chains. Additivity is an additional property needed for synchronized maximum distances.

The auxiliary `Additive` predicate replaces the chain inequality by equality.

import Lax544225.SemimetricSpace
import Mathlib.Order.Defs.PartialOrder

/-!

title: Ordered Semimetric Space
type: definition
---

$$a\leq b\leq c\quad\Longrightarrow\quad d(a,c)\geq d(a,b)+d(b,c).$$

# Formalization notes

The order is an explicit non-strict relation. Mathlib’s `IsPartialOrder` provides reflexivity, transitivity, and antisymmetry. The reverse triangle inequality is imposed only on ordered chains. Additivity is an additional property needed for synchronized maximum distances.

The auxiliary `Additive` predicate replaces the chain inequality by equality.
-/

universe u

namespace Lax544225.OrderedSemimetric

open SemimetricSpace
/-- The semimetric, partial-order, and ordered-chain distance laws. -/
def IsOrderedSemimetricSpace {S : Type u} (d : Distance S) (le : S → S → Prop) : Prop :=
  IsSemimetricSpace d ∧ IsPartialOrder S le ∧
    (∀ a b c, le a b → le b c → d a b + d b c ≤ d a c)

/-- Exact additivity of distance along the given ordered chains. -/
def Additive {S : Type u} (d : Distance S) (le : S → S → Prop) : Prop :=
  ∀ a b c, le a b → le b c → d a c = d a b + d b c

end Lax544225.OrderedSemimetric

concepts.title: (μ,ε)-Robustness of a Partition
concepts.description:
A partition is robust when each input has a nearby center whose entire robustness ball lies in the same part as that input.

**Definition from the paper.**

Let $(S,d)$ be a semimetric space. A partition $P:=\{S_1,\dots,S_p\}$ of $S$
is **globally robust** for $\mu\geq0$, $\epsilon>0$ if and only if

$$\forall x\in S\;\exists x'\in B(x,\mu)\;
\left[\bigvee_{i\in[p]}\bigl(\{x\}\cup B(x',\epsilon)\subseteq S_i\bigr)\right].$$

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
The parameter types encode μ ≥ 0 and ε > 0 directly: `μ : ℝ≥0` and `ε : ℝ>0`. Robustness and its only-trivial criterion take ε in this strictly positive subtype, without a separate positivity hypothesis. The robustness and separation predicates take explicit semimetric and partition evidence. Triviality of every robust partition quantifies over finite valid partitions. Separation uses a strict inequality because balls are closed.

The auxiliary separation predicate requires $\epsilon<d(x,y)$ for points in distinct parts.

import Lax544225.Partitions
import Lax544225.Balls

/-!
---
title: (μ,ε)-Robustness of a Partition
type: definition
---
A partition is robust when each input has a nearby center whose entire robustness ball lies in the same part as that input.

**Definition from the paper.**

Let $(S,d)$ be a semimetric space. A partition $P:=\{S_1,\dots,S_p\}$ of $S$
is **globally robust** for $\mu\geq0$, $\epsilon>0$ if and only if

$$\forall x\in S\;\exists x'\in B(x,\mu)\;
\left[\bigvee_{i\in[p]}\bigl(\{x\}\cup B(x',\epsilon)\subseteq S_i\bigr)\right].$$

# Formalization notes

The parameter types encode μ ≥ 0 and ε > 0 directly: `μ : ℝ≥0` and `ε : ℝ>0`. Robustness and its only-trivial criterion take ε in this strictly positive subtype, without a separate positivity hypothesis. The robustness and separation predicates take explicit semimetric and partition evidence. Triviality of every robust partition quantifies over finite valid partitions. Separation uses a strict inequality because balls are closed.

The auxiliary separation predicate requires $\epsilon<d(x,y)$ for points in distinct parts.
-/

universe u

namespace Lax544225.PartitionRobustness

open scoped NNReal

open SemimetricSpace Partitions Balls
/-- Coverage by monochromatic balls whose centers are μ-close to the input. -/
def MuEpsilonRobust {S : Type u} (d : Distance S) (hd : IsSemimetricSpace d)
    (P : Set (Set S)) (_hP : IsPartition P) (μ : ℝ≥0) (ε : ℝ>0) : Prop :=
  ∀ x, ∃ x', x' ∈ ball d hd x μ ∧ ∃ A ∈ P, x ∈ A ∧ ball d hd x' ε ⊆ A

/-- Distinct parts are separated by distance strictly greater than ε. -/
def Separated {S : Type u} (d : Distance S) (_hd : IsSemimetricSpace d)
    (P : Set (Set S)) (_hP : IsPartition P) (ε : ℝ≥0) : Prop :=
  ∀ A ∈ P, ∀ B ∈ P, A ≠ B → ∀ x ∈ A, ∀ y ∈ B, ε < d x y

/-- Every robust finite partition of the carrier has only the whole carrier as a part. -/
def OnlyTrivial {S : Type u} (d : Distance S) (hd : IsSemimetricSpace d) (μ : ℝ≥0) (ε : ℝ>0) : Prop :=
  ∀ P (hP : IsPartition P), MuEpsilonRobust d hd P hP μ ε → IsTrivial P

end Lax544225.PartitionRobustness

concepts.title: Partition and Classifier Induced Partition
concepts.description:
A partition divides a set into finitely many nonempty, disjoint parts. The trivial partition has just one part containing everything. A classifier induces a partition by grouping inputs with the same label.

**Definition from the paper.**

A collection of nonempty sets $\{P_1,\dots,P_p\}$ is a **partition** of a set
$S$ if and only if

1. $\bigcup_{i\in[p]}P_i=S$, and
2. $P_i\cap P_j=\emptyset$ for all $i\neq j$.

The partition $\{S\}$ on the set $S$ is called **trivial**.

A classifier $c:S\rightarrow[n]$ induces a partition
$P^c:=\{S^c_1,S^c_2,\dots,S^c_n\}$ with

$$S^c_i:=\{x\in S\mid c(x)=i\}.$$

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown: The family is a set of sets, so enumeration and duplicate parts are absent. Mathlib's `Setoid.IsPartition` supplies nonempty parts and unique membership. Finite families are required even when S is infinite.

import Lax544225.Classifier
import Mathlib.Data.Set.Finite.Basic
import Mathlib.Data.Setoid.Partition

/-!
---
title: Partition and Classifier Induced Partition
type: definition
---
A partition divides a set into finitely many nonempty, disjoint parts. The trivial partition has just one part containing everything. A classifier induces a partition by grouping inputs with the same label.

**Definition from the paper.**

A collection of nonempty sets $\{P_1,\dots,P_p\}$ is a **partition** of a set
$S$ if and only if

1. $\bigcup_{i\in[p]}P_i=S$, and
2. $P_i\cap P_j=\emptyset$ for all $i\neq j$.

The partition $\{S\}$ on the set $S$ is called **trivial**.

A classifier $c:S\rightarrow[n]$ induces a partition
$P^c:=\{S^c_1,S^c_2,\dots,S^c_n\}$ with

$$S^c_i:=\{x\in S\mid c(x)=i\}.$$

# Formalization notes

The family is a set of sets, so enumeration and duplicate parts are absent. Mathlib's `Setoid.IsPartition` supplies nonempty parts and unique membership. Finite families are required even when S is infinite.
-/

universe u

namespace Lax544225.Partitions

open Classifier
/-- A finite partition into nonempty parts with unique membership for every input. -/
def IsPartition {S : Type u} (P : Set (Set S)) : Prop :=
  P.Finite ∧ Setoid.IsPartition P

/-- The partition consisting of the whole carrier as its only part. -/
def IsTrivial {S : Type u} (P : Set (Set S)) : Prop := P = {Set.univ}

/-- The part assigned a particular classifier label. -/
def fiber {S : Type u} {n : ℕ} (c : Classifier S n) (i : Fin n) : Set S :=
  {x | c.label x = i}

/-- The collection of all label fibers. -/
def induced {S : Type u} {n : ℕ} (c : Classifier S n) : Set (Set S) :=
  Set.range (fiber c)

end Lax544225.Partitions

concepts.title: Precision Gap Metrics
concepts.description:
The precision gap measures compare distance with the number of ordered steps between two points. One measures the largest average distance per step; the other measures the largest number of steps per unit distance.

**Definition from the paper.**

Let $(S,<,d)$ be a finite totally ordered semimetric space with $|S|\geq2$.
For $a\leq b$, write $[a,b]:=\{x\in S\mid a\leq x\leq b\}$.
Define $\Delta$ and $\delta$ by

$$\Delta:=\max\left\{\frac{d(x,y)}{|[x,y]|-1}\;\middle|\;x,y\in S,\ x<y\right\},$$

$$\delta:=\max\left\{\frac{|[x,y]|-1}{d(x,y)}\;\middle|\;x,y\in S,\ x<y\right\},$$

where $|\cdot|$ denotes set cardinality.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown: The formulas take an ordered semimetric on a finite partially ordered carrier. The paper applies them to totally ordered carriers or pieces. The interval uses the ambient order of that carrier or piece. Natural cardinalities are cast into ℝ≥0 before division. Suprema of the finite ratio sets are their maxima. On a singleton the ratio sets are empty and Δ=δ=0, extending the paper’s undefined singleton case so decomposition pieces of size one need no arbitrary parameters. Δ equals the largest adjacent gap only for an additive distance; no such equality is presumed for general semimetrics.

import Mathlib.Data.Set.Card
import Mathlib.Data.NNReal.Defs
import Mathlib.Order.Interval.Set.Basic

/-!
---
title: Precision Gap Metrics
type: definition
---
The precision gap measures compare distance with the number of ordered steps between two points. One measures the largest average distance per step; the other measures the largest number of steps per unit distance.

**Definition from the paper.**

Let $(S,<,d)$ be a finite totally ordered semimetric space with $|S|\geq2$.
For $a\leq b$, write $[a,b]:=\{x\in S\mid a\leq x\leq b\}$.
Define $\Delta$ and $\delta$ by

$$\Delta:=\max\left\{\frac{d(x,y)}{|[x,y]|-1}\;\middle|\;x,y\in S,\ x<y\right\},$$

$$\delta:=\max\left\{\frac{|[x,y]|-1}{d(x,y)}\;\middle|\;x,y\in S,\ x<y\right\},$$

where $|\cdot|$ denotes set cardinality.

# Formalization notes

The formulas take an ordered semimetric on a finite partially ordered carrier. The paper applies them to totally ordered carriers or pieces. The interval uses the ambient order of that carrier or piece. Natural cardinalities are cast into ℝ≥0 before division. Suprema of the finite ratio sets are their maxima. On a singleton the ratio sets are empty and Δ=δ=0, extending the paper’s undefined singleton case so decomposition pieces of size one need no arbitrary parameters. Δ equals the largest adjacent gap only for an additive distance; no such equality is presumed for general semimetrics.
-/

universe u

namespace Lax544225.PrecisionGaps

open scoped NNReal

open SemimetricSpace OrderedSemimetric
/-- The number of consecutive steps between the endpoints of a closed interval. -/
noncomputable def steps {S : Type u} [PartialOrder S] (x y : S) : ℕ :=
  (Set.Icc x y).ncard - 1

/-- The largest average distance per ordered step. -/
noncomputable def deltaUpper {S : Type u} [Finite S] [PartialOrder S] (d : Distance S)
    (_hd : IsOrderedSemimetricSpace d (· ≤ ·)) : ℝ≥0 :=
  sSup {r | ∃ x y, x < y ∧ r = d x y / (steps x y : ℝ≥0)}

/-- The largest number of ordered steps per unit distance. -/
noncomputable def deltaInverse {S : Type u} [Finite S] [PartialOrder S] (d : Distance S)
    (_hd : IsOrderedSemimetricSpace d (· ≤ ·)) : ℝ≥0 :=
  sSup {r | ∃ x y, x < y ∧ r = (steps x y : ℝ≥0) / d x y}

/-- The paper’s precision-dependent obstruction threshold Δδμ+Δ. -/
noncomputable def threshold {S : Type u} [Finite S] [PartialOrder S] (d : Distance S)
    (hd : IsOrderedSemimetricSpace d (· ≤ ·)) (μ : ℝ≥0) : ℝ≥0 := deltaUpper d hd * deltaInverse d hd * μ + deltaUpper d hd

end Lax544225.PrecisionGaps

concepts.title: Semimetric Space
concepts.description:
A semimetric space is a nonempty set equipped with a symmetric, nonnegative real distance that is zero exactly on equal inputs. No triangle inequality is imposed.

**Definition from the paper.**

Let $(S,d)$ be a pair of a nonempty set and a function
$d:S\times S\rightarrow\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ such that, for all $x,y\in S$,

$$d(x,y)=0\iff x=y$$

(identity of indiscernibles) and

$$d(x,y)=d(y,x)$$

(symmetry). Then $(S,d)$ is a **semimetric space** and $d$ is a **distance**
function on $S$.

sections.markdown: The codomain ℝ≥0 supplies nonnegativity. The carrier is a type; nonemptiness is part of the predicate. Subspaces carry the restriction of the same distance.

namespace Lax544225.SemimetricSpace

concepts.sourceText:
import Lax544225.OrderedSemimetric
import Mathlib.Algebra.Order.BigOperators.Group.Finset

/-!
---
title: Sum Product Distance
type: definition
---
For tuples, add the distances between corresponding coordinates and compare tuples coordinate by coordinate. This preserves the ordered semimetric laws.

**Definition from the paper.**

If $(\mathcal F,<,d)$ is an ordered semimetric space, define

$$d_3(f,g):=\sum_{i\in[n]}d(f_i,g_i)$$

on $\mathcal F^n$, with the $n$-wise product partial order $<^n$.
Then $(\mathcal F^n,<^n,d_3)$ is an ordered semimetric space.

# Formalization notes

The construction is proved for any base carrier, including floating-point values. Coordinates are Fin n; the empty tuple has distance zero. The non-strict product relation includes equality; the paper’s strict notation denotes its strict part.
-/

universe u

namespace Lax544225.SumProductSpace

open SemimetricSpace OrderedSemimetric
open scoped BigOperators

/-- Coordinatewise order on finite tuples. -/
def productLe {S : Type u} (le : S → S → Prop) (n : ℕ) (f g : Fin n → S) : Prop :=
  ∀ i, le (f i) (g i)

/-- Sum of the base distances between corresponding coordinates. -/
noncomputable def sumDistance {S : Type u} (d : Distance S) (n : ℕ) : Distance (Fin n → S) :=
  fun f g => ∑ i, d (f i) (g i)

/-- Sum products preserve ordered semimetric spaces. -/
axiom statement {S : Type u} (d : Distance S) (le : S → S → Prop)
    (hd : IsOrderedSemimetricSpace d le) (n : ℕ) : IsOrderedSemimetricSpace (sumDistance d n) (productLe le n)

end Lax544225.SumProductSpace

      Lax544225.OrderedSemimetric.IsOrderedSemimetricSpace (Lax544225.SumProductSpace.sumDistance d n)
        (Lax544225.SumProductSpace.productLe le n)

sections.title: Proof strategy
sections.markdown:
Intersect a robust partition with a μ-closed piece and discard empty traces.
The traces form a robust partition of the induced subspace, hence are trivial.
Each piece is therefore monochromatic. A finite overlap chain propagates its
part to any input, forcing that part to be the whole carrier.

sections.title: Proof strategy
sections.markdown:
Use the absolute-distance proposition and closure of ordered semimetrics under
squaring. Squaring preserves symmetry, separation and the partial order. The
base antitriangle inequality bounds the sum of adjacent distances; its square
dominates the sum of their squares because both distances are nonnegative.

proofs.description: Theorem 3: cut covering is equivalent to covering from opposite boundaries.

sections.title: Proof strategy
sections.markdown:
Combine the two supporting implications. Between a covered within-side point
and an opposite-side center, choose a consecutive boundary crossing. The ordered
antitriangle law bounds distance to that boundary. To recover whole-ball
coverage, opposite-side points cover themselves with their own ε-balls.

sections.title: Proof strategy
sections.markdown:
Combine the two supporting implications. A robust center avoids the
ε-neighborhood of the complement of its part. Conversely, an uncovered μ-ball
supplies a center whose ε-ball stays within the selected part.

proofs.description: Theorem 2: only-trivial robustness is equivalent to coverage of every proper cut.

sections.title: Proof strategy
sections.markdown:
Combine the two cut arguments, using Theorem 1. An uncovered proper cut and its
complement give a nontrivial robust partition. In the converse direction, a
proper part of a robust partition contradicts coverage of that cut.

proofs.description: Synchronized finite maxima preserve the ordered semimetric laws.

sections.title: Proof strategy
sections.markdown:
A maximum vanishes exactly when every coordinate distance vanishes. Exact
base additivity makes synchronization transitive. On a nonempty synchronized
product the maximum equals any coordinate distance, giving exact chain
additivity; the empty product has distance zero.

sections.title: Proof strategy
sections.markdown:
Each proper cut has a consecutive crossing pair. SuccessorCovering places the
ball at the lower point inside an epsilon-ball centered on the opposite boundary.
Restrict this covering to the lower point's side and apply BoundaryExistence.

sections.title: Proof strategy
sections.markdown:
Use the finite ratio suprema to bound distance by Delta times interval steps and
steps by delta times distance. A successor adds exactly one interval step. On the
other side of the successor, the ordered antitriangle inequality gives monotonicity.

sections.title: Proof strategy
sections.markdown:
Zero sums force coordinate equality; symmetry and the antitriangle law follow
coordinatewise. The empty product is included by the same finite-sum laws.
